note: Gap between ί and the colon (~36 px in item) is at least as wide as the word space ἢ→π (~30 px) and ~3x the letter gaps; spaced colon (period French-style setting).
Heavy display type. The initial Α shows an enclosed counter above its crossbar; the 7th letter has no counter, solid apex and only an open space between the legs = Λ (ink-filled), not Α.
The mark top-right of Ψ is the curled top terminal of Ψ's own right arm (symmetrical with the left-arm terminal), separated from the lower arm by a break in worn type. No quote or apostrophe printed.

The odd glyph is ή set sideways (turned 90° clockwise): long bottom bar = η descender, short top bar = left stem with entry hook at top right, right vertical = the arch; the slanted dash after it is the rotated acute. Letter printed = η (misset), not α.

Descender clipped by the line crop. Visible part: wide letter (≈α width), curved left stroke with top hook running down-right and straight right stroke running down-left, crossing at the baseline = Porson-style χ; a γ would be narrower V. Fits σταχύω.
The mark at the start is the smooth breathing on ἀ (sits over α's left top), not a punctuation mark. Nothing printed before the word.
Full ΔΙΑΜΑΝΤΟΠΟΥΛΟΣ with Μ; a comma follows Σ at baseline (set slightly apart). Small specks below the line are noise.
Mark has a thicker head at top and a short tail turning down-left: comma-shaped apostrophe, not a straight wedge.
Rounded thick head with tail tapering down and slightly left (notch at left): curly comma-shaped apostrophe. The blob above it belongs to the line above.
α is clearly printed between θ and ι, so B is wrong. Gap before the raised asterisk is ~2/3 of the following word space: thin space at most; letters match A.
Mark is a curved stroke bulging right and ending slightly left at its foot (comma/right-quote curve), not a straight vertical tick; tilted, so it can look like a grave.
Clear comma-shaped apostrophe: round head on top, tail down-left.
ς→π gap ~5 px (line scale) equals ordinary letter spacing; real word spaces in the same line (στὸν τόπο) are ~12 px. Printed run together, like μας,ἰδίως in the same line.

Leading mark is a blob entirely above x-height (near cap height, at the clipped top of the line), too high for ano teleia and not «. Most consistent with the foot of an opening quote ‘ whose upper part is cut off by the crop; could be a stray dot.
Space after the period, then a long dash about two letter widths long (em dash). A has the space but an en dash; B has the em dash but no space.
A single curly closing quote (comma-shaped, head top, tail down-left) after the period, at the right edge of the crop; not », and not a straight '.
